sections.html:
Woodbury is one of the pricier east metro suburbs, eight miles east of St. Paul along Interstate 94 in Washington County. Most sales here involve newer houses and active buyers, with a short list of city rules about rentals and permits.

Because the houses are comparatively young, repair problems tend to be smaller than in older cities. The sellers who struggle are usually the ones with a tenant in place, an inherited house far from family, or a deadline that rules out a showing schedule.

Woodbury had an estimated 81,558 residents on July 1, 2025, up 8.6% from 75,105 in April 2020. It counted 61,961 people in 2010 and 46,463 in 2000, so the city has grown by about 75% since 2000. Figures for 2020 to 2024:

  • 29,312 households averaging 2.66 people
  • 77.6% of homes owner-occupied
  • Median owner-occupied home value: $450,200
  • Median monthly owner cost with a mortgage: $2,412
  • Median gross rent: $1,908
  • Median household income: $125,310

Families dominate, with 25.8% of residents under 18. High values mean a seller's equity is usually large, so the main question is speed and certainty rather than whether the sale clears the loan.

Woodbury covers 35.722 square miles, of which 34.895 are land. Interstate 94 forms the northern edge, 60th Street South the southern, Century Avenue the west and Manning Avenue the east. Neighbors include Oakdale, Lake Elmo, Cottage Grove, Maplewood, Newport and Afton.

Small lakes dot the city, including Powers, Wilmes, Colby and Carver. Woodbury maintains 63 parks covering about 3,600 acres and around 180 miles of mostly paved trails, which tends to be a selling point for houses near the lakes. Winters and summers are hard on roofs, gutters and furnaces, so expect buyers to ask about them. A quick look at the roof, the gutters and the furnace before you list can head off a price cut during the inspection.

Any single family home, townhome or condominium rented in Woodbury needs a city rental license, and the license expires December 31 each year. There is no exemption for owners with only one rental unit. Exceptions exist for family-occupied homes, nursing homes that hold a state license, some contract-for-deed sales while the buyer lives there, a fee waiver for owners on active military duty, and small residential settings with a state license.

Mid-year additions are pro-rated by quarter. A buyer who plans to keep a tenant should ask the Code Enforcement Division how the license transfers.

City code prohibits renting a property for a term shorter than 30 days when the renter's permanent residence is elsewhere. That matters for a buyer who is pricing a house on vacation-rental income, and for a seller whose listing history shows nightly bookings.

Tell any serious buyer about past short-term use up front. The disclosure rules ask sellers to share material facts they know, and a code violation fits that description.

sections.h2: Permits for fixing up a Woodbury house
sections.html:
Woodbury uses a combination permit system. One permit covers building, plumbing, heating and cooling, and electrical fees for additions, basement finishes, decks, porches, remodels, repairs and new construction. Stand-alone flat-fee permits cover single replacements such as a furnace, air conditioner, water heater, water softener or EV charger outlet, and they go to the contractor doing the work or to the homeowner.

  • Applications go through the city's online permitting portal.
  • Residential contractors must hold a valid Minnesota license or a mechanical bond.
  • Morning inspection windows run 9:30 to 11:30 a.m., so call by 9 a.m.
  • Afternoon windows run 1:30 to 3:30 p.m., so call by 1 p.m.

Call the Building Inspections Division at 651-714-3543 if you are unsure whether a project needs a permit. Finish and close any open permits before listing so a buyer's lender doesn't find them.

The deed is recorded with the Washington County Recorder. Minnesota's deed tax on a sale above $3,000 is .0033 of the net consideration under Minnesota Statutes 287.21, and it is due when the deed is presented for recording.

Your title company normally collects the tax and files the deed. Ask for the figure in the closing statement ahead of time, so you aren't surprised on the day.

Decide first whether the house is rented. If it is, confirm the rental license runs through December 31 and note what the buyer needs to do about the transfer. If the house hosted short stays, say so plainly in your disclosure. Close any open permits, then ask the title company for the deed tax figure and the Washington County recording details.

A listing adds showings and a buyer's loan. A cash sale skips them, and Woodbury's high values mean most owners have plenty of equity, so the timing question is mostly about certainty. Inherited houses and houses with a tenant are the usual cases where a buyer who takes the property as is saves the most time.

A traditional sale runs through showings, an offer, the buyer's loan approval and a lender's appraisal before the closing date is even set. A cash sale drops the loan and appraisal. The buyer's title company still checks the owner of record, any liens and the taxes, and the deed still gets recorded in Washington County, so the paperwork above doesn't go away. What goes away is the waiting on a lender.

For a seller with a tenant, an inherited house or a firm deadline, that can be the difference between a closing you can plan around and one that slips. For a seller with a clean, updated house and time, a listing may bring a higher price. Ask for both numbers before you choose, and compare what you would net after fees, repairs and the time the house sits.

Whichever route you pick, bring photo ID for every owner who signs, keep your rental license and permit papers together, and ask the title company early what it needs from you. Small gaps, such as a missing signature from a co-owner, are what usually delay a Woodbury closing.

faqs.q: Do I need a rental license to sell a rented house in Woodbury?
faqs.a: You need one to operate it as a rental until the sale closes. Single family homes, townhomes and condominiums rented in Woodbury all require a license, and the 2026 fee is $80 per unit.

faqs.q: Can a buyer run an Airbnb in Woodbury?
faqs.a: No. City code bans rentals under 30 days when the renter doesn't live there permanently.
Usually not. Owners complete a self-certification checklist each year, and the city inspects inside only for follow-up on a checklist item, an outstanding violation or a complaint.

faqs.q: How much is Minnesota deed tax on a Woodbury sale?
faqs.a: It is .0033 of the net consideration when the price is above $3,000, and it is due when the deed is presented for recording. Your title company normally collects it.

faqs.q: Which county records a Woodbury deed?
faqs.a: Washington County. Contact its recorder's office for current filing fees, and confirm with your title company who will submit the paperwork.
